#2659. AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

At the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect."

The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he said.

President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

"A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he said. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty."

While Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress said during the company's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

"That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he said.

Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

"[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "big trouble."

"Now that he's back, they're not," he said.

Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

"Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy said in a note Monday.

Nvidia said on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

"These issues have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," said economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

"The company is doing everything in its power to execute," he said. "They don't need the high yield market at this time."

In the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a probe. At the federal level, President Trump said Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

"There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg said. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file."

#2656. Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson, Ben Roethlisberger among players advancing in Hall of Fame voting process

The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced the names of 52 players who have advanced to the next round of voting for possible enshrinement as part of the Class of 2027.

The group includes five players who are in their first year of eligibility. They are tight end Rob Gronkowski, running back Adrian Peterson, quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, wide receiver Antonio Brown, and cornerback Richard Sherman.

After changes to the selection process this year, there are no longer Modern and Senior candidates in the player pool. The group of 52 players will be cut to 25 in the next round of voting and then 13 finalists will be selected from that group. They will join Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft in the final pool of eligible candidates with the selection committee selecting a group of between three and seven members.

#2654. Donovan Mitchell on 9-9 Cavs' inconsistent effort: 'I'm trying to figure out how not to end up on ESPN'

The Chicago Bulls entered Thanksgiving week as one of the NBA's worst teams: 4-12, getting outscored by nearly eight points per 100 possessions, with the second-worst defense in the NBA. And yet, they controlled the bulk of Monday's matchup with the Cleveland Cavaliers, leading for nearly the entire final three quarters — and by as many as 24 points — in a 122-108 win.

This, despite the Cavs coming in with a rest advantage, with the Bulls on the second night of a back-to-back after going to overtime against the Nuggets on Sunday. And despite Chicago being without leading scorer Norman Powell, who's stuck in street clothes nursing a strained right hamstring, and 2026 lottery pick Caleb Wilson, out with a broken right hand. And despite a pair of Chicago starters — point guard Josh Giddey and swingman Matas Buzelis — getting benched, again, late in the fourth quarter by first-year head coach Tiago Splitter, who elected to close with backup point guard Tre Jones and intriguing two-way reserve Jaylin Sellers. (Giddey did not seem particularly pleased about that.)

And, perhaps most importantly, despite the Cavs … well, frankly, they're just supposed to be better than this.

Donovan Mitchell (right), James Harden and the Cleveland Cavaliers have stumbled to .500 a month into the season.

Yes, Cleveland's without Evan Mobley, an integral component of its operations on both sides of the floor. And yes, Kenny Atkinson's club wound up on the business end of Chicago going 20-for-49 from 3-point range while the Cavs made just eight of their 31 triple tries. Not exactly easy to win when you're outscored by 36 points from long distance.

It's not just the simple, cruel vicissitudes of shooting variance, though. Aside from Mobley, the Cavs had the entire rest of their preferred rotation against a four-win team … and they still got drilled. A Cleveland squad that made it to the Eastern Conference finals last spring enters Wednesday's matchup with the New York Knicks — the team that, as you might recall, annihilated the Cavs in that series en route to winning the NBA championship — at 9-9, in seventh place in the East.

That's a long way from where the Cavs — one of the most expensive rosters in the sport — want to be … and, from the sound of things, they've got some pretty big questions to answer before they can get there. From Danny Cunningham of The Inside Shot:

Donovan Mitchell, who had a game-high 28 points, was asked about the effort being inconsistent from quarter-to-quarter or game-to-game this season.

Mitchell thought for a full five seconds after the question was asked.

"I think," he said before pausing for eight more seconds. "I'm trying to figure out how not to end up on ESPN."

"I think the biggest thing now is just figuring each other out. We're not here in the locker room panicking, and all I can say to that, is what we got going forward. Nights like tonight are bad. It's a bad night, and we got to respond to that. We've got to respond to that and just keep playing our game. There's so many different things you can point to, but at the end of the day for us, it's within us. I have all the confidence in everybody in here, and we've got all the confidence in each other. We've got to go out there and execute it. That doesn't really answer your question, but yeah."

If there's one thing I'm qualified to assess as a longtime professional blogger, it's this: That was a lot of words to not really make any point or address the issue at hand. Which, come to think of it, might constitute a pretty loud statement about the state of affairs in Cleveland right about now.

Mitchell wasn't the only Cavalier searching for an answer to the issues that have characterized the club's fits-and-starts opening to the season. Peyton Watson, the swingman who came over from Denver in an offseason sign-and-trade intended to plug Cleveland's long-yawning hole on the wing, offered a somewhat more direct answer than the All-NBA scoring guard.

"I think if we knew the answer, we would just do it," Watson said in the locker room. "I think we're still searching for that. You know, I'm always trying to communicate with my teammates and try to help make their job easier and just be a guy that connects the team in a lot of ways. I think I try to just go out there and lead by example by playing as hard as I can every night. I just think that everybody has got to look inward and look themselves in the mirror and ask themselves, 'Am I giving it 100% every single night?' I think that if that's not the case, then we need to go to the drawing board and really, like I said, look in the mirror and evaluate ourselves."

That doesn't exactly seem like the most stirring vote of confidence for the competitive makeup of the Cavaliers, especially considering they've already gone through a few moments that would seem to invite such sober self-reflection.

Blowing a 29-point lead against the 76ers on opening night. Dropping both ends of a home-and-home to the post-injury-apocalypse Thunder. Getting boat-raced by the Knicks in the second half at home, an extension of the pain of the conference finals. Getting blown out by a Hornets team playing without Brandon Miller or Kon Knueppel. Getting out-executed down the stretch by a Grizzlies squad playing without Ty Jerome. And now, Monday's scattershot effort in Chicago.

It just feels like something's missing in Cleveland, some spark, some urgency — and it starts on the defensive end.

The last half-decade of success for the Cavs — a climb out of the post-LeBron basement that began with the Mobley/Allen/Darius Garland unit under J.B. Bickerstaff, and that continued after the trade for Mitchell made it a "core four" — had been predicated on consistently stout defenses, with Cleveland ranking in the top eight in points allowed per possession each season from 2021 through 2025. That began to shift when Atkinson's arrival supercharged the offense, and more firmly tilted after dealing for Harden; Cleveland posted a top-five offense after the trade deadline, but a below-average defense, and got routinely torched by the Knicks in the four-game conference finals sweep.

The Cavs now sit at 21st in defensive efficiency — on pace for their first bottom-10 finish on that end since 2020-21. They're conceding shots at the rim and from beyond the 3-point line more regularly, and they give up wide-open 3s at a bottom-10 rate. (Nearly half of Chicago's 3-point attempts on Monday came without a Cavalier defender within 6 feet of the shooter.) They don't force turnovers, and they're average-at-best at clearing the defensive glass and guarding without fouling. That's a recipe for underwhelming results, unless you can balance out that bottom-10 defense with a No. 1-with-a-bullet offense … which the Cavs, currently a good-but-not-overwhelming seventh in points scored per possession, don't have at the moment.

Maybe they will. Get Mobley healthy, get Harden — who followed up his 51-point Friday masterclass by shooting 5-for-14 from the floor with seven turnovers in Chicago — more consistently off the schneid, and get Watson (a career-low 48% on 2-pointers and 27% on 3s) thawed out, and maybe these Cavs have the ingredients they need to build on last season's trip to the final four and put themselves in position to make a bid to represent the East in the NBA Finals. They believe they have the talent to do that.

Right now, though, they feel like a team that's less than the sum of its parts — a group that's playing like it's just kind of going through the motions until the real season starts, rather than one that needs to earn its postseason spot in an East that's gotten more crowded at the top. And if the Cavs want to have a shot at being the last team standing come springtime, they need to start finding answers as fall turns to winter.

"You can't just turn it on in April or May," Cavs guard Sam Merrill told reporters. "I think building the right habits only makes it easier to play that way once you get to later in the season and in the playoffs. We continue to talk about it. That's got to continue to be our mindset."

Talking about it is one thing. Their next chance to do something about it comes Wednesday in New York. One bit of good news for Mitchell and Co., at least? The game won't air on ESPN.

#2648. Three former Falcons advance in Pro Football Hall of Fame voting

The voting process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2027 is underway, as the Hall continues to narrow down its list of candidates ahead of February's NFL Honors.

On Tuesday, the Hall announced that 52 players have advanced to the next round of voting, with three former Atlanta Falcons among them, all of whom are deserving of a spot in Canton: Tommy Nobis, John Abraham and Billy "White Shoes" Johnson.

It's long overdue for "Mr. Falcon" to receive his gold jacket. The first-ever draft selection in franchise history, Nobis spent his entire 11-year NFL career with the Falcons from 1966-1976.

Nobis was named NFL Rookie of the Year in 1966, earned five trips to the Pro Bowl and was named to the NFL's 1960s All-Decade Team, despite entering the league midway through the decade. He led the Falcons in tackles in nine of his 11 seasons and was an inaugural member of the Falcons Ring of Honor in 2004. His No. 60 jersey is also retired by the franchise.

One of the best pass rushers in franchise history, Abraham spent seven seasons with the Falcons from 2006-2012, recording 68.5 sacks during his time in Atlanta, which remains an official franchise record.

Abraham finished his 15-year NFL career with 133.5 sacks, five Pro Bowl selections and two first-team All-Pro selections. "The Predator" recently received some well-deserved recognition from the franchise, as he was inducted into the Falcons Ring of Honor in October.

One of the most electrifying return specialists in NFL history, Johnson spent six seasons with the Falcons from 1982-1987. In 1983, Johnson earned his third career Pro Bowl selection and was named NFL Comeback Player of the Year. He also led the Falcons in receptions in both 1983 and 1985.

Perhaps most baffling is the fact that Johnson remains the only player named to the NFL's 75th Anniversary All-Time Team who has yet to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He was also named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team, as well as the 1970s and 1980s All-Decade Teams.

The list of 52 nominees will be narrowed down to 25 following the next round of voting, with the results expected to be announced in approximately two weeks. Hopefully, all three former Falcons will find themselves one step closer to football immortality in Canton, Ohio.

In fact, ESPN just recently named their top potential All-Star participants, and Sengun was listed in the top four. Here's what they had to say about Alpie:

"Trivia time: Who is the leading scorer for the NBA's most efficient offense?

Somehow, the answer is Sengun, who is posting a career-best 22.1 points per game for a balanced Rockets attack that has all five starters averaging in double digits.

While Fred VanVleet's return from injury has shifted Kevin Durant into a slightly lower-usage role, the 24-year-old Sengun has remained a central part of Houston's offense. That center is obviously Sengun's idol Nikola Jokic. But Sengun is having a very Jokic-like season, averaging 21.9 points now, 9.2 rebounds, 7 assists and 1 steal per game. Sengun is shooting 55.1 percent from the field and is shooting 50 percent on triples while putting up 2 attempts per game. It's not a full breakout due to Houston's egalitarian offense, but Kevin Durant's willingness to take a back seat has been good for Sengun and the Rockets.

Speaking of KD, ESPN thinks he's on track for his 17th NBA All-Star appareance, as he's having himself another fine year. He had a season-high 32 points in last night's win over the Clippers, and ESPN had this to say about everyone's favorite Twitter burner holder:

The field for the West's final two All-Star spots has been thinned out by injuries to Edwards, Lakers guard Austin Reaves, Spurs guard Dylan Harper and the Thunder's Jalen Williams and Holmgren. From that group, Reaves is best positioned to make a speedy return and claim a spot.

For now, Durant narrowly edged out Minnesota's Gobert, Portland's Lillard and Phoenix's Devin Booker. The 38-year-old forward has ceded some authority in Houston's offense but has maintained 51/40/88 shooting splits and a healthy plus-8.3 net rating.

The quality of Durant's contributions remains high, even if his 21.0 points per game are the fewest since his rookie campaign. Houston's league-leading offense, which ground down in last year's playoffs, needs Durant's gravity to thrive, and he has led the Rockets in minutes despite being by far the team's oldest player."

KD is now averaging 21 points per game to go along with 5.4 rebounds and 3.8 assists, while shooting 51 percent from the floor and 42 percent from deep. Again, KD's willingness to take a slight back seat in Houston's pecking order has been good for the development of the offense, and KD has shown he can still step up when needed, which was the entire point of getting KD to begin with. It wasn't for him to be a heliocentric one-man show like he was often last season.

Houston stands at 13-5 and in fourth place in the Western Conference. They are currently on a 59-win pace. It sure would be some NBA season if 59 wins gets you only to the fourth, but my guess is this current standings bunch-up starts to thin out here pretty soon. But with two All-Stars like Sengun and KD in the mix, the Rockets will be in the thick of things either way.

#2641. Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Antonio Brown among players advancing in Pro Football Hall of Fame voting process for 2027 class

A pair of quarterbacks from the fabled 2004 draft class, Pittsburgh Steelers legend Ben Roethlisberger and New York Giants icon Eli Manning, plus embattled wide receiver Antonio Brown, are among the 52 players the Pro Football Hall of Fame revealed are advancing in the voting process for the 2027 class.

Per current Hall of Fame bylaws, at this stage of that process, selectors cast ballots for 50 players they believe should move forward in their candidacy, but those tied for the 50th position also remain eligible for induction.

The list the Hall announced on Tuesday will next be cut down to 25 players. That more exclusive group will be unveiled in about two weeks.

For now, here's a position-by-position breakdown of the players being considered for enshrinement:

Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Ken Anderson

Shaun Alexander, Frank Gore, Marshawn Lynch, LeSean McCoy, Adrian Peterson, Fred Taylor, Ricky Watters

Anquan Boldin, Antonio Brown, Rob Gronkowski, Torry Holt, Billy "White Shoes" Johnson, Steve Smith Sr., Otis Taylor, Hines Ward, Reggie Wayne, Jason Witten

Rodney Harrison, Lester Hayes, Albert Lewis, Eddie Meador, Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas III, Everson Walls, Darren Woodson

John Abraham, Geno Atkins, L.C. Greenwood, Jim Marshall, Robert Mathis, Haloti Ngata, Vince Wilfork, Kevin Williams

Maxie Baughan, London Fletcher, James Harrison, Karl Mecklenburg, Tommy Nobis, Terrell Suggs

Roethlisberger and Manning draw the eye, considering they each quarterbacked historic franchises to a pair of Super Bowl victories; however, this cohort is understandably littered with household names.

Running back Adrian Peterson is forever part of Minnesota Vikings lore. He's one of the nine NFL players to ever rush for 2,000 yards in a season. In fact, Peterson's 2,097 yards on the ground in 2012 were the second most in single-season league history, behind only the 2,105 rushing yards Eric Dickerson logged while starring for the Los Angeles Rams in 1984. Peterson earned NFL MVP honors that season.

Another RB in the running, Frank Gore, is the NFL's third all-time leading rusher. Gore spent the bulk of his career with the San Francisco 49ers. Even in his 16th and final campaign, he was still somewhat productive, amassing 653 rushing yards in his age-37 season with the New York Jets back in 2020.

Rob Gronkowski and Jason Witten are both integral to the annals of tight end play. Gronkowski was a red-zone monster, finishing his 11-season career with a whopping 92 receiving touchdowns. Together, he and seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback Tom Brady authored one of the most electrifying duos in the sport, first with the New England Patriots and then with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As for Witten, he proved to be one of the NFL's most reliable security blankets to date, maxing out with 110 catches during his 2012 campaign with the Dallas Cowboys.

Interestingly, beleaguered wideout Antonio Brown was among the players included in 52-man list the Hall put forth on Tuesday. Brown was a superstar during the peak of his head-scratching 12-season run in the league. He built most of his résumé in Pittsburgh, where he stacked seven 1,000-yard receiving seasons. In his nine-season stay with the Steelers, he led the NFL in receiving yards twice: first in 2014 and again in 2017. He also led the league in touchdown catches in 2018.

But the end of Brown's career was marred by the trouble he got himself into, on and off the field. Earlier this month, in a Miami court, Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault following a 2025 shooting incident.

Brown still has long odds of being inducted next year. Ultimately, 13 players will make up most of the 15 finalists who will be presented at the selection committee's annual meeting. The other two candidates will be Bill Belichick (who emerged from the "coach" category) and Patriots owner Robert Kraft (who came out of the "contributor" category).

The Hall's 2027 class will be announced at "NFL Honors" in February.

#2638. From College Tennis to the PPL: Guille Jiménez Cagigas on Growing Padel in America

During my time writing about the U.S. padel scene, I've run into a ton of folks who came to this country to play college tennis and who are now driving the growth of padel here. The latest of these fellows is Guillermo "Guille" Jiménez Cagigas. After a distinguished junior tennis career in Spain, Guille played five seasons of tennis at Longwood University in Virginia, where he rose to the number one singles spot in his final season. He transitioned to padel and is currently ranked No. 8 in the 2026 USA Padel Circuit standings. In addition to playing for the Smash and elsewhere, he co-founded the padel performance training company PadelEdge. As a former member of USA Padel's Junior Development Committee (2024), he has a unique vantage point on the growth and expansion of padel, especially junior padel, in this country.

Guille was in Las Vegas last week to represent the hometown Las Vegas Smash in the PPL's regular-season finale at Dolby Live. It was a tough week. He and partner Agustín Torre got routined in both of their matches, and the Smash came up a point short of qualifying for the PPL Finals next week in Miami. Luckily, I sat down with him before the start of the event, and he was in a fine mood. I wanted to get his take on where the U.S. stands from a padel development standpoint and how long it will be before we dominate padel like we dominate World Cup soccer and Olympic bobsled.

The latest of these fellows is Guillermo "Guille" Jiménez Cagigas. After a distinguished junior tennis career in Spain, Guille played five seasons of tennis at Longwood University in Virginia, where he rose to the number one singles spot in his final season. As a former member of USA Padel's Junior Development Committee (2024), he has a unique vantage point on the growth and expansion of padel, especially junior padel, in this country.

Guille was in Las Vegas last week to represent the hometown Las Vegas Smash in the PPL's regular-season finale at Dolby Live. It was a tough week. He and partner Agustín Torre got routined in both of their matches, and the Smash came up a point short of qualifying for the PPL Finals next week in Miami. Luckily, I sat down with him before the start of the event, and he was in a fine mood. I wanted to get his take on where the U.S. stands from a padel development standpoint and how long it will be before we dominate padel like we dominate World Cup soccer and Olympic bobsled.

Q: Give me your impression of padel in the United States right now. Are we just starting out? Are we years away from producing top-level players?

In my opinion, we are in the early beginning, early stage of padel, especially if we're talking about junior development and having our own stars from like a young age. We are 10, 15 years away from that at least. But it's great that projects like the PPL and all these things are happening and we're bringing talent from where the sport is already huge so it can become the same here, no? And all of those players, they come from Spain, they come from Europe, from Argentina, and it's what's gonna make the sport bigger here.

#2637. Dan Quinn on Stefon Diggs: I love his fire

#2623. Steve Kerr, Erik Spoelstra top list of highest paid NBA coaches

In 2024, when the Warriors and Steve Kerr agreed to a two-year extension paying him $17.5 million a season, other coaches celebrated — he had driven up the market price overall for coaches.

While other coaches' salaries may have climbed, Kerr remains the highest-paid coach in the league, according to Kurt Badenhausen of Sportico, who did the research on coaching contracts (which are not publicly available). Here are the top 10 highest-paid coaches, all making eight figures a year:

Steve Kerr (Warriors): $17.5 millionErik Spoelstra (Heat): $15 millionTyronn Lue (Clippers): $15 millionRick Carlisle (Pacers): $11 millionIme Udoka (Rockets): $11 millionJoe Mazzulla (Celtics): $11 millionMike Brown (Knicks): $10 millionQuin Snyder (Hawks): $10 millionTaylor Jenkins (Bucks): $10 millionDusty May (Mavericks): $10 million

A few thoughts from the Sportico research:

• Kerr, Spoelstra, and Lue also happen to be the NBA's three longest-tenured head coaches with their current teams.

• Jenkins and May were hired this summer with those eight-figure salaries, with Dallas paying up to get May out of Michigan (where he had just won a national championship). They got hired at higher salaries than established, very successful coaches such as Mark Daigneault in Oklahoma City and Chris Finch in Minnesota.

• The story reports the standard starting salary for an NBA head coach is at least $4 million a season. Two coaches are below that number: Doug Christie in Sacramento, and Micah Nori in Portland, who is on a much-discussed (and despised by other coaches and basketball people) one-year deal with less than $2 million guaranteed, and with options after it. With what Nori has done with the Trail Blazers so far, he deserves a reward of stability (and more cash).

Pittman was downgraded to out for Week 2 after the team's final practice of Week 2 on Saturday, Sept. 19. Pittman did not practice on Thursday or Friday after first being limited in practice with an injury on Wednesday, Sept. 17.

Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman Gennings Dunker at minicamp on June 3, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Rookie offensive lineman Gennings Dunker did not play against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, and remains on the injured reserve list. Dunker had originally been listed as questionable to play, but was not activated by the Saturday deadline.

Dunker had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday, Nov. 18, and he was a full participant in practice all week.

Dunker was placed on injured reserve on Saturday, Sept. 26, and was to miss four to six weeks with an MCL sprain. Dunker had previously been ruled out of the team's Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Dunker suffered a knee injury at practice on Thursday, Sept. 24, and did not practice on Friday, Sept. 25. He had been a healthy scratch in Weeks 1 and 2.

Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Nick Herbig in a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Outside linebacker Nick Herbig was ruled out against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11 with rib and hip injuries. Herbig had originally been listed as questionable, but was downgraded to out after the team's practice on Saturday, Nov. 21.

Herbig was a full participant in practice on Friday, Nov. 20. He did not practice for the Steelers on Wednesday, Nov. 18 or Thursday, Nov. 19 with rib and hip injuries. It's unclear when he suffered the injuries.

Herbig played about 10% less snaps than his season average in the team's Week 10 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, despite the Steelers defense spending almost the entire game on the field.

Herbig played in 28 snaps of defense and 12 snaps of special teams on Sunday.

Second-year outside linebacker Jack Sawyer will replace him as the team's No. 3 pass rushing option. KJ Henry was elevated from the practice squad.

Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick is carted off during the team's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Guard Mason McCormick was placed on the Steelers' injured reserve list on Wednesday, Nov. 18. He is expected to miss at least eight weeks with a dislocated ankle that will not require surgery.

McCormick was injured just before halftime of the Steelers loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15. Trainers placed an air cast on his lower right leg and he was carted off the field.

Spencer Anderson replaced McCormick in the Steelers' starting offensive line.

Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Defensive tackle Sebastian Joseph-Day was placed on the injured reserve list on Thursday, Oct. 22. He will miss at least the team's next four games.

Joesph-Day did not practice on Wednesday, Oct. 22. It's unclear when he suffered the injury. Joseph-Day played a season-high 26 snaps of defense against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18.

Yahya Black will become the team's top backup defensive tackle in the sub-package alignment, with Gabriel Rubio the top backup in base defense.

Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman Jack Driscoll walks off the practice field on Aug. 24, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Offensive lineman Jack Driscoll was placed on the injured reserve list, designated to return, on Aug. 30. He will miss at least the first four games of the season.

Driscoll was not dressed for practice during the portion of the session open to the media on Tuesday, Aug. 25. Driscoll had walked off the practice field with a member of the training staff during the portion of practice that was open to the media on Monday, Aug. 24, and returned with his ankle taped.

Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Logan Lee at training camp on Aug. 3, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Steelers defensive tackle Logan Lee was placed on the injured reserve list on Thursday, Aug. 13, which will end his 2026 season unless he reaches an injury settlement with the team.

Lee had missed seven straight practices before being placed on IR. The nature of Lee's injury has not been disclosed.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Cole Burgess at training camp on July 30, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Cole Burgess reverted to the Steelers' injured reserve list on Wednesday, Aug. 5. He will be out for the remainder of the season, unless he reaches an injury settlement with the team.

Burgess suffered a significant knee injury during training camp practice on Monday, Aug. 3, and was carted off the field at St. Vincent College. On Tuesday, Aug. 4, he was waived with an injury designation.

Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Donte Kent at rookie minicamp on May 9, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now

Donte Kent will begin the season on the PUP list, meaning he will miss at least the first four games. Kent was running off to the side on his own during the team's first training camp practice on Wednesday, July. 29. He was first placed on the PUP list on Tuesday, July 28.

Kent missed his entire rookie season with the Steelers in 2025 with a pair of injuries. He suffered a calf/ankle injury in training camp, and then as he opened his practice window in an attempt to return, Kent suffered an ACL injury that caused him to miss the rest of the season. Kent was a limited participation in spring practice.

Inside linebacker Patrick Queen played through a broken thumb against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11.

Queen was a full participant in practice on Friday, Nov. 20. He was limited in practice for the Steelers on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and Thursday, Nov. 19 with a hand injuries. It's unclear when he suffered the injury.

Queen played every snap of the Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Queen is expected to be able to play through the broken thumb.

Strong safety DeShon Elliott played against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11.

Elliott was a full participant in practice on Thursday, Nov. 19, for the first time since re-injuring his knee, and also on Friday, Nov. 20. Elliott had been limited in practice for the Steelers on Wednesday, Nov. 18.

Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warmups before the Steelers played the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15.

He had previously been dealing with an ankle injury and a year-long knee/hamstring injury.

Wide receiver Roman Wilson was activated from the injured reserve list on Saturday, Nov. 21 and returned to action against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11 on Nov. 22.. He had originally been listed as questionable.

Wilson had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday, Nov. 18, and he was a full participant in practice all week.

Wilson was placed on injured reserve on Saturday, Oct. 17 and will miss at least four games with a finger injury.

Wilson had been ruled out of the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday, Oct. 12.

Wilson left the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11, late in the first half with a left hand injury. Wilson hurt his hand attempting to make a catch on his lone target of the game. He was originally ruled to have caught the ball, but it was reversed on review. Wilson was seen after the game with his left hand in a large wrap.

Rookie Germie Bernard, who had been playing outside receiver in place of Michael Pittman Jr, moved inside to fill in for Bernard, with Brandon Smith playing outside.

Cornerback Doneiko Slaughter had no Week 10 injury status and played against the Cincinnati Bengals. Echols was a full participant in practice all week, as he returns from a hamstring injury.

Slaughter was ruled out of the Steelers' Week 8 game against the Cleveland Browns. Slaughter did not practice all week with a left hamstring injury.

Slaughter suffered the injury while covering a punt in the fourth quarter of the Steelers' 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Oct. 25.

If Slaughter misses time, he will likely be replaced by veteran cornerback Terrell Smith.

Cornerback Brandin Echols had no Week 10 injury status and played against the Cincinnati Bengals. Echols was a full participant in practice all week, as he returns from a hamstring injury.

Echols was ruled out of the Steelers' Week 8 home game against the Cleveland Browns. He did not practice at all that week.

Echols was ruled out of the team's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints, the team announced on Thursday, Oct. 22, and he did not travel with the team to Paris. Skowronek did not participate in either of the team's first two practices.

Echols suffered the hamstring injury in the first half of the Steelers' Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He left the game and did not return.

Ben Skowronek had no Week 10 injury status and played against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Skowronek said he was healthy and ready to go for Week 10 after being listed as a full participant in practice on Wednesday, Nov. 11. He was also a full participant on Thursday, Nov. 12 and Friday, Nov. 13.

Skowronek did not play after being listed as questionable to play against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8.

Skowronek returned to practice in a limited capacity for the first time on Wednesday, Oct. 28, as he works back from a calf injury, and was limited once again on Thursday, Oct. 29 and Friday, Oct. 30.

Skowronek was ruled out of the team's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints, the team announced on Thursday, Oct. 22, and he did not travel with the team to Paris. Skowronek did not participate in either of the team's first two practices.

He had also been ruled out of the Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday, Oct. 12.

Skowronek left the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11, late in the first half with a calf injury.

Skowronek was injured in the second quarter, was treated in the sideline medical tent, and then went straight to the locker room. He did not return to the sideline in the second half.

Brandon Johnson was elevated from the practice squad to replace Skowronek.

Safety DeShon Elliott did not have a Week 10 injury status and was expected to play against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Elliott popped back up on the team's injury report on Wednesday, Nov. 11, as he was limited with an ankle injury. He was a full participant on Thursday, Nov. 12 and Friday, Nov. 13.

Elliott had declared himself fully healthy in Week 8, after missing nearly an entire year with a serious hamstring/knee injury. He played 24 snaps against the Cleveland Browns, an increase from his first game back, but nowhere near a full workload.

Derrick Harmon was activated from the injured reserve on Saturday, Nov. 14 and returned to action against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Harmon was questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bengals, as he attempted to make his return from a foot injury. He was a full participant in practice on Friday, Nov. 13.

Harmon had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday, Nov. 11, when he was listed as a limited participant in practice. He was also limited on Thursday, Nov. 12.Harmon said he's 100% healthy, but the team is still taking it day-by-day on whether he'll play in Week 10.

Harmon was placed on injured reserve on Monday, Oct. 5, and by rule, had to miss at least four weeks with his left foot injury. Week 10 is the first week he is eligible to return.

Harmon left his team's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday, Oct. 2. Harmon left the game in the second quarter and was carted off the field. He was later seen at Huntington Bank Field wearing a protective boot.

Strong safety DeShon Elliott said he's fully healthy on Wednesday, Oct. 28 and could play a full game if needed in Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns.

Elliott played limited snaps in his return from injury against the New Orleans Saints in Week 7. He was removed from the injured reserve list on Saturday, Oct. 24 after being listed as a full participant in practice for the third straight day on Friday, Oct. 23.

The previous week, Elliott limited participant in practice for the fifth straight session on Friday, Oct. 16 and was ruled out of a Week 6 return.

Elliott had his 21-day practice window opened and was a limited participant in practice on Thursday, Oct. 8. He was again a limited participant on Friday, Oct. 9, but was ruled out for a Week 5 return.

Elliott suffered an aggravation of a his 2025 hamstring injury after making his return to game action in the Steelers' second preseason game against the New York Jets on Aug. 21.

Defensive back Jalen Ramsey will once again play against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8 and does not have an injury status for the game.

Ramsey was a full participant in practice on Thursday, Oct. 29 and Friday, Oct. 30. He did not practice on Wednesday, Oct. 28, as the Steelers continue to manage his reps as he plays through a fractured right wrist.

Ramsey played against the New Orleans Saints on Oct. 25, and did not have an injury status for the game. He was listed as an estimated full participant in the team's hotel walkthrough on Friday, Oct. 23. Ramsey was limited in practice on Thursday, Oct. 22 after missing practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

Ramsey played against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7 after being listed as questionable. He was limited in practice on Thursday, Oct. 15 and Friday, Oct. 16 after not practicing on Wednesday, Oct. 14.

Ramsey played against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6 after he was listed as questionable. He had been limited in practice on Thursday, Oct. 8 and Friday, Oct. 9 and did not practice on Wednesday, Oct. 7.

Ramsey played in Week 4 after being listed as questionable and being limited in all three of the team's practices. He had his arm in a sling for Monday's practice, but ditched the sling for a cast on Tuesday.

Ramsey played every defensive snap for the Steelers in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals despite breaking his wrist early in the game.

Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith returned to play in full against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8.

Highsmith was listed as limited in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 28 and Thursday, Oct. 29, as he continues to fight through a groin injury.

Highsmith played against the New Orleans Saints in Week 7 and did not have an injury status after being listed as an estimated full participant in the team's hotel walkthrough in Paris on Friday, Oct. 23.

Highsmith was limited in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21 and Thursday, Oct. 22.

Running back Rico Dowdle played after being listed as questionable to play against the New Orleans Saints in Week 7 with a knee injury. Dowdle rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught six passes for 45 yards, and did not appear to be hampered by the injury.

Dowdle was listed as a limited participant in practice for the third straight day on Friday, Oct. 23. Dowdle was first listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21 with the knee injury.

Dowdle played against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18 after being listed as questionable with a previous toe injury.

Dowdle was a full participant in practice on Thursday, Oct. 15 and Friday, Oct. 16, but remained questionable to return against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He had been a limited participant in practice for the fourth straight session on Wednesday, Oct. 14.

Dowdle did not play in Week 5 after being listed as questionable. He was limited in all three sessions leading up to the week.

Dowdle did not play in the Steelers' Week 4 game against the Cleveland Browns after missing all three practice session of the week. He was also ruled out of the Steelers' Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Dowdle suffered the toe injury in the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots. He initially left the game, and was listed as questionable, before attempting to return. But Dowdle eventually exited again and was ruled out.

Travis Homer and Lew Nichols replaced Dowdle in the rotation at running back with Jaylen Warren.

Outside linebacker T.J. Watt played against the New Orleans Saints in Week 7 without an injury designation. He was listed as an estimated full participant in the team's Paris hotel walkthrough on Friday, Oct. 23.

Watt was added to the Pittsburgh Steelers injury report on Thursday, Oct. 22 with a calf issue as the team got ready to travel to Paris for its.

Watt did not practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21 but that absence  was listed as just for rest purposes. He was limited in practice on Thursday with the calf injury. Watt was in the locker room after practice, and did not seem to be visibly hobbled by the injury.

Defensive tackle Keeanu Benton played after being questionable to dress against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He was a full participant in practice on Friday, Oct. 16.

Benton missed practice on Wednesday, Oct. 14 and was limited on Thursday, Oct. 15. It's not clear when or how Benton suffered the injury. He did not suffer an obvious injury during the team's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

Tight end Pat Freiermuth played despite being questionable against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18.

Freiermuth suffered a calf injury in practice on Saturday, Oct. 17 and was added to the team's official injury report for Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with a questionable designation.

Wide receiver DK Metcalf had his injury status removed and he was cleared to play in the Steelers' Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Metcalf missed practice on Friday, Oct. 16 with an illness and has been listed as questionable to face Tampa Bay, but was cleared on Saturday.

Cornerback Jamel Dean played after being questionable against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18. He was a limited participant in practice for the third day in a row on Friday, Oct. 16, as he returned from an ankle injury.

Dean might not miss as much time as initially thought with the aggravation of an ankle injury that he suffered against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4. Dean left the game in the first half and was seen in a walking boot afterward.

NFL Network reported on Sunday, Oct. 4 that Dean is expected to miss multiple weeks with the injury. Head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday, Oct. 5 that Dean will be evaluated on Wednesday, Oct. 6, and will not be placed on injured reserve at this time.

McCarthy said on Thursday, Oct. 8 that Dean is feeling better than they expected, and Dean himself said he's targeting a Week 6 return.

Dean apparently suffered an ankle injury in the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, and he missed some snaps near the end of the game.

Dean dressed and started after being listed as questionable to play against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. Dean did not participate in the team's first practice of Week 3 on Wednesday, Sept. 23, but was listed as limited in the final two practice sessions of the week.

Cornerback Brandin Echols was a full participant in all three practices leading up to the team's Week 5 home game against the Indianapolis Colts and suited up in that game. Echols played in Week 4 after being listed as questionable and being as limited in all three of the team's practices.

Echols left the Steelers' Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals while being evaluated for a potential concussion. He cleared the NFL concussion protocol on Wednesday, Sept. 30.

Echols hit Bengals kick returner Ke'Shawn Williams facemask-to-facemask while attempting to secure a muffed punt. He was first evaluated on the sideline before being taken to the Steelers locker room. He did not return to the game.

Daylen Everette replaced Echols as the Dime defender.

Running back Jaylen Warren dressed and started after being listed as questionable to play against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. Warren was limited in all three of the team's practices of the week.

Warren apparently suffered a shoulder injury in the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, but finished the game without issue.

If both Warren and Dowdle miss time, the Steelers will likely call a up a running back from the practice squad.

Troy Fautanu was not listed on the team's injury report for Week 3, and started against the Cincinnati Bengals. He was a full participant in all three practices.

Fautanu played despite being listed as questionable in Week 2. He was a full participant in practice on Friday, Sept. 16 after being a limited participant in practice on Thursday, Sept. 17 after missing the team's first session of the week on Wednesday, Sept. 16.

Fautanu had a player roll up the back of his ankle during the fourth quarter of the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

Dylan Cook moved to left tackle and Max Iheanachor played right tackle while Fautanu was out.

Offensive lineman Spencer Anderson is dealing with a minor fracture in his leg, but was not listed on the team's injury report for Week 3, and was a full participant in all three practices. He was dressed for the game against the Bengals, but was one of two dressed players to not suit up.

Anderson apparently suffered the injury in the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, but he did not miss any playing time in the game.

It appears that Brock Hoffman could be in line to replace Anderson in the lineup at right guard, regardless of his injury status.

Ben Skowronek returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Skowronek was cleared from the concussion protocol and was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Skowronek is expected to play in Week 1.

Skowronek left the team's preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills in the first quarter, after making a tackle on a kickoff. He was immediately taken to the Pittsburgh locker room and did not return to the game.

Will Howard returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Howard was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9.

Howard was cleared from the concussion protocol, and was a participant in the team's padded practice at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on Thursday, Sept. 3.

Howard reported concussion symptoms after playing in the first half of the Steelers' preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27.

Sebastian Joseph-Day returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Joseph-Day was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Joseph-Day first participated in the team's unpadded practice on Wednesday, Sept. 2.

He was not dressed for practice on Tuesday, Aug. 25, while dealing with an oblique injury that also held him out of the team's first two preseason games. He did not play in the preseason finale on Aug. 27. There is no specific timetable for his return.

Yahya Black stepped up as the No. 4 defensive lineman in his absence.

Fullback Riley Nowakowski returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Nowakowski was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Nowakowski suffered an ankle injury during the Steelers' preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills.

Safety Jaquan Brisker returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

Brisker was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Brisker did not participate in any of the team's three preseason games.

He suffered some type of injury late in practice on Friday, Aug. 7, and was not dressed when the Steelers traveled to Latrobe Memorial Stadium for their night practice on Saturday, Aug. 9. Brisker dressed and took part only in individual periods on Monday, Aug. 10.

Robert Spears-Jennings moved into the starting lineup with Brisker out.

Linebacker Payton Wilson returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

Wilson was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Wilson was not dressed for the portion of practice open to the media on Tuesday, Aug. 25 with an undisclosed injury, and did not participate in the team's preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27.

Wilson was not wearing pads and was a limited participant in practice on Monday, Aug. 24. Wilson played in the team's second preseason game against the New York Jets on Friday, Aug. 21, and played in 18 snaps without apparent issue.

Cole Holcomb replaced Wilson in the starting lineup while he was out.

Jalen Ramsey returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

Ramsey was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Ramsey once again practiced on Tuesday, Aug. 25, after being activated from the physically unable to perform list, but did not participate in the team's final preseason game against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27.

Ramsey was placed on the PUP list with a knee injury on the first day of training camp. Ramsey had been running off to the side running training camp practices. Ramsey suffered a minor knee injury toward the end of the team's minicamp. The injury did not require surgery.

Brandin Echols replaced Ramsey in the team's starting lineup.

Michael Pittman Jr. returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

Pittman was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Pittman was dressed for practice and was a limited participant on Tuesday, Aug. 25.

Pittman had not been active since he apparently injured his right leg during a 7-on-7 period in the team's practice at Latrobe Memorial Stadium on Aug. 8.

Germie Bernard replaced Pittman in the starting lineup.

DK Metcalf returned to action in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

He was a full participant in the team's first practice of Week 1 on Wednesday. Metcalf returned to practice in a limited capacity in Monday. Aug. 24, but did not participate in the team's preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27.

Metcalf suffered an undisclosed injury during the team's Saturday night practice at Latrobe Memorial Stadium on Aug. 8.

Max Iheanachor returned to action in the Steelers preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27. He had practiced for the second straight day on Tuesday, Aug. 25, after missing two and a half weeks with an apparent neck/shoulder injury.

Iheanachor left the Steelers' practice after the first full-speed team period on Thursday, Aug. 6. He walked to the sideline, where head athletic trainer Gabe Amponsah appeared to be working on his neck and right shoulder area. Iheanachor then had a conversation with Dr. Aaron Mares, one of the team's physicians, and left the practice field, walking up the hill.

Iheanachor was back dressed for Steelers practice on Monday, Aug. 10, even after McCarthy said that he would not take part in the practice session. Iheanachor did not participate in any team periods, but did do some individual work. He did not return to practice until Aug. 24 after that.

Broderick Jones replaced Iheanachor as the second-team right tackle, with Jack Driscoll bumping up to the second team at left tackle.

Slot cornerback Brandin Echols returned to action in the Steeles preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27. He was dressed for practice on Tuesday, Aug. 25 as a limited participant.

Echols did not participate in either of the team's first two preseason games and was also dressed but not in pads during his team's practice on Wednesday, Aug. 19.

Echols came down awkwardly on his left ankle while jumping for a pass alongside Roman Wilson on Thursday, Aug. 6. Echols limped off the practice field and had a large wrap on his left ankle.

On Monday, Aug, 10, Echols had the walking boot off his injured left ankle. He had been seen with the walking boot on Saturday, Aug. 8.

Rookie cornerback Daylen Everette returned to play in the Steelers' preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills. He practiced in pads for the second straight day on Tuesday, Aug. 25 and told Steelers Now that he was feeling good to go after a minor injury. Everette suffered an undisclosed injury and was not dressed in pads for the team's practice at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on Wednesday, Aug. 19, and he missed the team's Week 2 preseason game against the New York jets as a result.

Safety Israel Mukuamu was released on Monday, Aug. 24 with an injury settlement.

Mukuamu left practice near the end of the team's training camp practice on Saturday, Aug. 15, walking up the hill from Chuck Noll Field with team trainers, nursing an undisclosed lower-body injury.

Mukuamu did not participate in the team's preseason game against the New York Jets on Aug. 21, and was not seen participating during the portion of practice open to the media on Wednesday, Aug. 19.

Kaden Wetjen was a full participant in practice for the second straight practice session on Wednesday, Aug. 19, and he returned to game action against the New York Jets on Aug. 21. Wetjen missed practice on Saturday, Aug. 15 with a left ankle ailment, and was working off to the side with trainers during practice periods.

Keeanu Benton was in the starting lineup for the Steelers' preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday, Aug. 13. He had returned to practice in team periods on Monday, Aug. 11, and did not have the large wrap on his right hand/wrist during practice. Benton had been limited in practice since about Friday, Aug. 8, and has been seen with a large wrap on his right wrist. Benton had still been active in individual periods, and also has been running off to the side.

Eli Heidenreich played 25 snaps in his preseason debut on Thursday, Aug. 13, after shaking off a right hamstring injury. He was back at practice in a full capacity on Tuesday, Aug. 11, after he returned to practice in a limited form on Monday, Aug. 10. Heidenreich missed the previous three sessions with a right hamstring injury.

#2611. Bills see two practice-squadders poached by other teams

The Buffalo Bills suddenly have two vacant spots on their practice squad.

Core pieces of said practice squad, quarterback Shane Buechele and 2025 sixth-round pick Chase Lundt, were added to the 53-man rosters of other teams in separate transactions on Tuesday before the club's Week 12 Thanksgiving contest against the Chiefs.

Given the Colts released Daniel Jones on November 20, they were in need of more quarterback depth behind former first-rounder Anthony Richardson, who's become the team's starter. Buechle is presumed to be Indianapolis' new No. 3 quarterback behind Richardson and Riley Leonard.

Buechele spent from 2023 – 2025 with the Bills before re-signing in Buffalo in January 2026.

Under 20 minutes later, it was reported that Lundt was on the move too:

The Seahawks are dealing with injuries to newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson, longtime right tackle Abraham Lucas, and franchise left tackle Charles Cross.

The former sixth-round pick failed to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills but played over 300 preseason snaps the past two summers after a collegiate career at UConn.

Who do you think the Bills should add to their practice squad after losing Buechele and Lundt?

#2610. Fantasy Basketball Week 5 takeaways: Wemby's historic dominance, key injuries and more from all 30 teams

A quick fantasy basketball breakdown on all 30 teams after Week 5 of the 2026-27 NBA season.

Spurs: Victor Wembanyama dominated Saturday: 50 points, 19 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals in 32 minutes of a 114-91 win over the Pelicans. It got him the High Score of the week, with 97 fantasy points. He's the first player since 1973-74 with a 50/15/5/4 game (since steals and blocks became official stats). It's his second 50 piece this month (52 on Nov. 4), and San Antonio is 15-3 on the season with Wemby leading the way as the top player in fantasy.

Bulls: Josh Giddey posted 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists in Sunday's 151-145 OT loss to Denver, the league's first 20-20 game this season. Giddey followed up that epic game with a 2-for-11 performance with 4 points, 11 assists, 2 stocks and 3 turnovers on Monday. He was benched in crunch time (again). If you have Giddey, I'd sell. The game-to-game variance is too erratic.

Heat: Bam Adebayo posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists with zero turnovers in Sunday's 123-113 win over OKC with Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) out. Miami has won seven straight to reach 10-6. Shout-out to Klay Thompson, who averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 3s over a recent seven-game stretch and is closing in on Ray Allen for third all time in 3s. Keep holding Klay in 12s.

Bucks: Tyler Herro set a new career high in Philly on Saturday, dropping 50 points, then added 32 with 8 assists in Monday's win in Toronto to snap a 13-game skid. At 2-16, start prepping for some shakeups in the rotation — which could impact vets like Herro, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. Rookie Brayden Burries (40% rostered) had 14 points, 10 boards, and 4 assists off the bench Monday, and should be rostered in most leagues.

Cavaliers: James Harden dropped 51 in Friday's 128-119 win over Indiana, passing Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games ever (26). Evan Mobley (toe) has missed six straight and is due for re-evaluation this week. Kenny Atkinson has started Tyrese Proctor and Sam Merrill over the past week, but rookie Meleek Thomas (13.3 points in 24 minutes) is still the best streamer here.

Nets: Nolan Traore (right hamstring) will be re-evaluated in 8-10 weeks. Mikel Brown Jr. (19% rostered) got the first crack, starting Monday in Minnesota with his minutes restriction lifted: 17 points, a career-high 7 assists and 5 boards in 29 minutes. Egor Demin shot 3-for-13 off the bench. Brown is the add over Demin. The No. 6 pick has a path to 30 minutes a night.

Lakers: Austin Reaves (left heel) practiced fully on Sunday and is targeting a return on Friday in San Antonio. Quentin Grimes averaged 9.2 points through 12 games, then moved into the starting lineup over the last five games, averaging 24.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.4 assists. He ranks 31st in 9-cat over that span, with 35.58 fantasy points per game.

Enjoy it now, because he won't see anywhere near 37 minutes a night when Reaves returns. Matisse Thybulle is the keeper. His 39 steals rank second in the league, and he and Wemby are the only players this year with 15+ blocks, 20+ steals and 30+ 3s.

Hawks: Atlanta has won four straight without CJ McCollum, whose left calf strain will be re-evaluated in about four weeks. No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings got next, but don't rush to get him because the Hawks won't play until Friday.

Dyson Daniels, though? He's such a unique fantasy talent. He's posting 9.5 points, 7.4 boards, 5.6 assists and a league-leading 2.9 steals per night. He can't shoot beyond 10 feet, but he's touching nearly every major counting-stats category except blocks and 3s.

Grizzlies: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. That hurts. Kris Murray started in his absence on Monday, playing 32 minutes and got 5 stocks. Add him to the watchlist, even though Memphis will likely form a committee between Murray, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant (when he gets back). Make sure Cam Spencer (45%) isn't on waivers.

Clippers: Brandon Ingram started in his debut Monday in Houston and posted 16 points, 7 boards, and 4 assists in 27 minutes. The shooting was unsurprisingly rough (6-for-18, 0-for-6 from three), but 18 shots in his first game since May is a great sign. Marc Stein reported that LA is showcasing vets like Rui Hachimura and Kris Dunn before the trade deadline.

Jazz: Svi Mykhailiuk went OFF Sunday for 39 points and 10 threes, both career highs. I'd rather pick up Ace Bailey, though.

76ers: Philly's five-game win streak ended Monday against Portland with Joel Embiid (illness) out. Embiid's been better, and fantasy managers could take the opportunity to float offers because health is always the biggest question mark with Embiid.

Celtics: Four straight losses. Derrick White is shooting 40.1% from the field and 28.8% from 3, well off his 45.4/38.7 peak. I'm holding in 9-cat, but it's been a disappointing start.

Mavericks: Just two games this week, and two scheduled before the NBA Cup next week. Cut fringe Mavs for players who play more games over the next two weeks.

Knicks: Josh Hart is averaging 6.6 points on 34/27/60 shooting. Woof.

Pistons: Over the past five games, Ausar Thompson ranks 16th in 9-cat. He's making 87.5% of his free throws (albeit low volume, but still!)

Magic: Anthony Black continues to lap Jalen Suggs. Suggs is averaging 9-5-4 with 35/29/73 shooting splits. He's down to 73% rostered, but fantasy managers should stay patient as he ramps up from a bone bruise injury that cost him eight games.

Wizards: The Wizards want Trae Young to focus less on scoring and more on passing. Per Kevin O'Connor, Young had 8 minutes of possession time per game over his first 6 games. It's down to 5 minutes over his last 5 games.

Raptors: Toronto lost to the 2-16 Bucks and sits at 6-11 overall. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is shooting at practice but is still a couple of weeks away from returning. Jakob Poeltl is back on the radar after averaging 11.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.3 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game in his last three games.

Pacers: At 5-12 without Tyrese Haliburton, Indiana is reportedly looking to make a move. In the meantime, Kelly Oubre Jr. (36%) should be rostered in all leagues.

Hornets: Brandon Miller and Coby White sat all of OT in a four-point loss to the Lakers last week. Minutes restrictions are costing teams Ws.

Timberwolves: Rudy Gobert ranks 114th in points leagues and 290th in 9-cat. His efficiency near the rim is pacing to his worst since his rookie season — he's 17-for-53 on layups through Monday. Plus, his rebounding and block rates are tumbling. Keep an eye on Joan Beringer.

Rockets: At 13-5, Houston owns the NBA's best offensive rating (121.1) and a plus-8.2 net rating (5th in the league).

Nuggets: Nikola Jokić logged triple-double No. 202 on Sunday. He's seven behind Russell Westbrook's record.

Trail Blazers: Donovan Clingan is finishing 74% at the rim, up from 66% last season.

Thunder: Nearly 80% of Ajay Mitchell's shots are 2s and he's hitting 28.3% from 3. He'll need to extend that range if the Thunder want to right the ship.

Suns: Four straight wins after Monday's OT victory in New Orleans. If Jalen Green was dropped in a points league, pick him up.

Warriors: Stephen Curry (oblique) is due for re-evaluation this week.

Pelicans: New Orleans sits at 5-14, so it's a team to watch by the deadline. Keep holding the young guys, Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. Everyone else could be on the block.

Kings: Keegan Murray has 12-plus points and seven-plus boards in four of his last five. Rounding into form? Maybe.

#2599. Michigan does about-face on Trev Alberts, potentially owing him $17.2 million

The last time Trev Alberts made this kind of a stir, he was the subject of Bill Tobin’s legendary rant against Mel Kiper.

This time, the situation potentially involves a significant payment to Alberts.

Via ESPN, Michigan backed out of an agreement to hire Alberts (who played in only 29 career games over three seasons after being the fifth overall pick in the 1994 draft) to become the university’s next athletic director. Alberts told ESPN that he had signed a “binding memorandum of understanding” for the position.

Alberts’s lawyer, Tom Mars, told ESPN that Michigan owes Alberts a $17.2 million buyout.

For that kind of money, Michigan will be very tempted to refuse to pay, forcing litigation and the expense, uncertainty, and delay that goes along with it. Alberts could decide to take less than he’s owed, simply to end the fight.

Of course, Alberts also could become determined to prove a point — if he and Mars believe Alberts has an ironclad claim to the money.

Michigan’s about-face apparently relates to deposition testimony from Alberts in a Title IX case arising from his tenure at Nebraska. Per ESPN, Alberts gave testimony on December 4, 2025, that Michigan regards as problematic.

Alberts was asked whether he believes it’s true that college coaches should never have sex with the athletes they’re coaching. The obvious answer is, “Yes.” Alberts pursued a different strategy.

“I don’t know the answer to that,” Alberts said.

“Well, I mean, you know, it just depends,” Alberts replied.

He then said the situation could be “nuanced,” due to preexisting relationships or eligibility waivers that could result in athletes being nearly the same age as young assistant coaches.

It’s an example of the gamesmanship in which some witnesses will engage when grilled by lawyers during depositions. The lawyer wanted to get an admission from Alberts that could be used broadly, and repeatedly, in the case arising from a relationship between a women’s basketball player and an assistant coach. Alberts tried to resist by clumsily splitting hairs.

Then there’s the question of whether Michigan is genuinely troubled by the testimony, or whether the school is using it as a way to justify not hiring Alberts — and not paying him.

Whatever happens between Alberts and Michigan, it’s another example of the so-called “chaos” in college sports being not the result of players doing their best in trying to get paid but schools doing their worst in allocating resources.

If Michigan’s concerns about the testimony are legitimate and not a pretext for hiring someone else, it shows that Michigan engaged in poor vetting of Alberts before signing him to a memo of understanding. If it’s a pretext, it shows that Michigan made a hasty decision and then tried to justify a change by trumping up testimony that otherwise wouldn’t have been an issue for Michigan.

Regardless, the possibility that Michigan will owe Alberts all or part of $17.2 million is another tangible example of the fact that the “chaos” comes not from players making good decisions but from schools making bad ones.

#2597. NFL Injury Report, Week 12: Latest news, updates for Kenneth Walker III, Brock Bowers, more players for fantasy football

It's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule. The Packers and Rams play Wednesday night, while we have the usual three-game Thanksgiving lineup. We also have the Broncos and Steelers on Black Friday, then the normal Sunday slate and Monday Night Football.

So Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers. We're here to help out, taking you through the NFL injury report with the latest updates and some fantasy analysis for key players.

Justin Herbert, LAC (concussion protocol)

Drake Maye, NE (leg) — Out at least six weeks

Herbert: The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively. Herbert turned in his first QB1 finish of the 2026 season with 22.44 fantasy points against the Jets on Sunday. He only had 131 passing yards, two TDs, 32 rushing yards and another score on the ground, so it isn't like "we are so back" or anything. But now Herbert will need to clear concussion protocol in order to play Week 12 against the Patriots, another solid matchup.

With how the QB landscape is right now, if Herbert can clear, he isn't a bad add as a QB2 or streaming option for Week 12. The Chargers have some winnable matchups down the stretch and Herbert will likely need to throw. Maybe Herbert and the Chargers can still salvage something for fantasy.

Darnold: The reigning Super Bowl champ has missed the past two games but has a shot to get back on the field for Week 12 against the 49ers in a big spot. Seattle is coming off its bye and Drew Lock has been the starter. He's been more than serviceable, undefeated in essentially four starts this season. There's not much difference between Darnold and Lock starting for fantasy managers. Whoever starts will be a QB2 this week, and either way, Jaxon Smith-Njigba will get fed.

Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Unlikely to play in Week 12

J.K. Dobbins, DEN (suspension) — Won't play in Week 12

Walker: The Chiefs' lead back missed his second straight game Sunday, though the team didn't miss him much. Kansas City rolled to another easy win over the Cardinals, 34-7. Emmett Johnson led the backfield again with another strong performance, racking up 143 total yards, four catches and a score for 22.3 fantasy points. Johnson has RB1 finishes in three of his past four games.

The Chiefs take on the Bills in a highly anticipated matchup on Thanksgiving night. Walker will have a short week to get ready to return, which isn't ideal. If Walker sits again, Johnson can be fired up as an RB1 in what should be a high-scoring affair. If Walker is able to play, we could see him eased back into action given how well Johnson has fared in his stead. In that scenario, Walker would return to RB1/2 status while Johnson would hold value as a flex play.

Tuten: The Jaguars took a tough loss in Week 11 to the Giants and lost Tuten late in the game with an undisclosed injury. He had been dealing with an ankle issue coming into the contest, so it could have something to do with that. Either way, Tuten has been playing pretty banged up over the last handful of games.

If Tuten ends up missing Week 12, Chris Rodriguez Jr. would likely take over the backfield. He had four carries for 28 yards against New York, and has four rushing TDs on the season. C-Rod would basically be elevated to RB2 status with a matchup against the Titans in Week 12. If Tuten is active, you have to play him but know there's some risk given the injuries.

Davante Adams, LAR (hamstring) — Out until at least Week 13

Bowers: The Raiders were without their top offensive weapon for a loss to the Broncos on Sunday afternoon in Week 11. It felt like a long shot for Bowers to be ready but there's optimism he'll be back for Week 12 against the Browns. Fernando Mendoza looked better in his second NFL start, which is encouraging for Bowers' fantasy prospects. If Bowers is active, you're playing him. If he's out, there aren't any teams on bye, so there should be plenty of streaming options, including Michael Mayer, though he was quiet with just one catch for four yards on Sunday.

Kincaid: It's been another up-and-down, injury-impacted campaign for the Bills' tight end. He missed his first game of the season in Week 11 against the Dolphins but had been popping up on the injury report most weeks. Since his hot start, Kincaid only had one game with double-digit fantasy points in the past seven games. Dawson Knox got a few catches against Miami but isn't really a viable streaming option if Kincaid is out again for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.

#2596. Panthers Need Four Wins To Lock NFC South Title

The Carolina Panthers beat the Baltimore Ravens 35-33 on Sunday night at Bank of America Stadium. This win puts the team back at .500 for the season. Every other team in the division sits at 3-7 right now. That gap looks big, but the road ahead is full of traps. The Panthers have seven games left on their schedule. Four of those are against teams outside the division. The other three are against division rivals who are desperate to catch up.

A win against Tampa Bay on Monday night changes the whole math for the season. Per Cat Scratch Reader, the Panthers might only need three wins to clinch the division title if they beat the Buccaneers. That game happens at Raymond James Stadium. It is a tough spot to play. The Buccaneers have an easier schedule than Carolina does. They only face one team with a winning record for the rest of the year. That opponent is the Rams in Week 17. If the Panthers lose on Monday, the pressure will mount fast. The tiebreaker rules would then favor Tampa Bay. The Panthers would need to create distance quickly to stay safe.

Most fans and analysts think four wins are the magic number to lock up the playoff spot. This is a high bar for a team with a mixed record. The remaining non-division games are the biggest test. The Panthers play the Vikings on the road and the Steelers away. They also host the Bengals and the Seahawks. With a 6-4 record, the Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions. The other three teams are in the playoffs, while the Seahawks are out of the postseason picture. Beating any of these teams is a hard task.

Division games are the key to the title race. The Panthers play one game against each of the other NFC South teams. The Saints can make up ground on Tampa Bay in their upcoming game against the Cardinals. If the Panthers sweep the division, it creates the most distance possible. To overtake Carolina straight up, someone would have to win out. That is a very tall order for the Saints or the Falcons. The math favors Carolina if they stay healthy.

The game on Monday, Nov. 30 is the most important one left on the schedule. It starts at 8:15 p.m. ET. The Panthers travel to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers. A win here sets the tone for the final stretch. A loss forces the team to win more games than planned to stay ahead. If the Panthers lose that game, they will face pressure to build a lead over Tampa, which has a simpler schedule and a tiebreaker advantage. For that to happen, the easiest way is for the Panthers to sweep the division.
